_about: Shared by every industry: the three closes and the objection buttons. An industry file can override any node or objection by using the same id. Paths like "@quick" point at that industry's anchors.

close.question: Wrap up: pick the close
say: This has been really helpful, thank you.
From what you've told me, a few things are costing you real time: {{pains}}.
And if one thing ran itself, you said it'd be {{wish}}.
close.why: The highlighted close is a suggestion based on how many pains you tagged. Trust your ear over the count.

close_audit.question: Book the $750 audit
say: Here's what I'd suggest. I do a flat $750 operations audit. I sit with you for about an hour, map how a lead becomes a {{finishLine}}, and hand you a one-page report of where time and money are leaking and how to fix it.
First thing I'd look at: {{topPain}}.
If you have me build the fix within 30 days, the $750 comes off the price.
Would Tuesday or Thursday work?
close_audit.why: Ask for a specific day. 'Sometime next week' is a callback, not a booking.
checklist: Lock a date and time, and send the invite while you're still on the phone
Ask who else should be there (ops manager, office, PM)
Ask them to have their job list or spreadsheet open for the session

close_callback.question: Schedule a callback
say: Totally fair. Sounds like there might be something here, but now's not the moment.
When's better, later this week or early next?
I'll send a quick invite so it doesn't get lost.
close_callback.why: Pin an exact time. An open-ended 'call me later' almost never gets answered.
checklist: Pin an exact day and time
Confirm the best number and email
Write down which pain to lead with next time (in Notes)

close_exit.question: Polite exit
say: No problem at all, I appreciate you giving me a couple of minutes.
If things like {{topPain}} ever start costing you more, mind if I check back in a few months?
Have a good one.
close_exit.why: Leave on good terms. The 'no' today is often a 'yes' in six months.
checklist: Note why: not a fit, bad timing, or already handled
Ask: anyone else you know I should talk to?

too_busy.label: Too busy
say: Totally get it. Busy is exactly when things slip, and that's who I work with.
Give me 60 seconds and one question. If it's not relevant, I'll let you go.
too_busy.why: Ask for a tiny, bounded slice of time. It respects them and usually gets a yes.

have_software.label: We already have software
say: Great, most of the folks I work with do. Most people use about 20% of what they're paying for.
I'm not selling software. Half my audits are 'set up what you already pay for', plus fixing the handoffs between tools where someone re-types things or a job sits waiting.
Can I ask: does it talk to the rest of your setup?
have_software.why: Agree, then move to the gaps between tools. That's where the pain usually is.

paths.label: Ask about the gaps between tools

how_much.label: How much is it?
say: Fair question. It starts with a flat $750 audit, about an hour, and you get a one-page report of what's leaking and how to fix it.
If you want me to build the fix, builds run $5–8k, and the $750 comes off that price if you go ahead within 30 days.
But I'd rather find out if there's anything worth fixing first. Can I ask a couple more questions?
how_much.why: Give the price straight. Dodging it kills trust. Then go back to discovery.

paths.label: Wants to think, book a callback

send_email.label: Send me an email
say: Happy to, and I'll keep it short.
So it's actually useful and not generic: what's the one thing you'd want it to answer?
And what's the best email?
send_email.why: 'Send me an email' is often a polite brush-off. Asking for the one thing turns it back into a conversation.

paths.label: Got the email, follow up in 2 days

not_interested.label: Not interested
say: No problem, I appreciate you being straight with me.
Can I ask: is it that things are running pretty smoothly, or just not the right time?
not_interested.why: This separates 'no need' from 'no time'. The second one is a callback.
